    # Read the colored marks at crossings of the regular separator lines.
    # The repeated background stripes establish the spacing; the output is
    # the compact pattern of the marked crossing array.
    bg = max(set(v for row in grid for v in row), key=lambda x: sum(row.count(x) for row in grid))
    row_marks = [r for r in range(h) if sum(v != bg for v in grid[r]) > 0]

def transform(grid):
    h, w = len(grid), len(grid[0])
    from collections import Counter
    counts = Counter(x for row in grid for x in row)
    background = counts.most_common(1)[0][0]

    # The encoded picture is at intersections of the regularly spaced
    # separator stripes. Locate rows and columns that are predominantly
    # separator-colored (not the tile background).
    separator = max((x for x in counts if x != background),
                    key=lambda x: counts[x])
    rows = [r for r in range(h)
            if sum(x == separator for x in grid[r]) > w // 2]
    cols = [c for c in range(w)
            if sum(grid[r][c] == separator for r in range(h)) > h // 2]

    a = [[background if grid[r][c] == separator else grid[r][c]
          for c in cols] for r in rows]

    # Repeated lattice rows/columns encode the same output cell; collapse
    # adjacent duplicates, then remove the blank outer margin.
    b = []
    for row in a:
        if not b or row != b[-1]:
            b.append(row)
    a = b
    if a:
        keep = []
        for j in range(len(a[0])):
            col = [row[j] for row in a]
            if not keep or col != [row[k] for row in a for k in []]:
                pass
        # Collapse adjacent duplicate columns.
        selected = []
        prev = None
        for j in range(len(a[0])):
            col = tuple(row[j] for row in a)
            if col != prev:
                selected.append(j)
                prev = col
        a = [[row[j] for j in selected] for row in a]

    while len(a) > 1 and all(x == background for x in a[0]):
        a.pop(0)
    while len(a) > 1 and all(x == background for x in a[-1]):
        a.pop()
    while a and len(a[0]) > 1 and all(row[0] == background for row in a):
        for row in a:
            row.pop(0)
    while a and len(a[0]) > 1 and all(row[-1] == background for row in a):
        for row in a:
            row.pop()
    return a

def transform(grid):
    h, w = len(grid), len(grid[0])
    # Detect full separator stripes by their dominant color and periodicity.
    row_counts = [max(set(row), key=row.count) for row in grid]
    # Separator rows are the unusual rows whose majority color differs from
    # the tile color used on the ordinary rows.
    ordinary = [row_counts[r] for r in range(h)
                if row_counts.count(row_counts[r]) > 1]
    tile = max(set(ordinary), key=ordinary.count) if ordinary else row_counts[0]
    sep_rows = [r for r in range(h) if all(v == row_counts[r] for v in grid[r])
                and row_counts[r] != tile]
    # For each separator row, marker values interrupt its separator color.
    sep_cols = [c for c in range(w)
                if sum(grid[r][c] == tile for r in range(h)) > h // 2]

    if not sep_rows or not sep_cols:
        return [[tile]]
    # Keep separator intersections, turning unmarked separator cells into
    # the ordinary tile color. Trim only completely unmarked outer bands.
    out = [[tile if grid[r][c] == row_counts[r] else grid[r][c]
            for c in sep_cols] for r in sep_rows]
    while len(out) > 1 and all(x == tile for x in out[0]):
        out.pop(0)
    while len(out) > 1 and all(x == tile for x in out[-1]):
        out.pop()
    while out and len(out[0]) > 1 and all(row[0] == tile for row in out):
        for row in out:
            row.pop(0)
    while out and len(out[0]) > 1 and all(row[-1] == tile for row in out):
        for row in out:
            row.pop()
    return out

def transform(grid):
    # Sample the colored lattice at horizontal/vertical separator crossings.
    # The regular input background tiles are 1s; separator lines are 9s.
    h, w = len(grid), len(grid[0])
    # Marked horizontal separator rows are the rows containing colors other
    # than 1 or 9; preserve the full sequence of 3-cell tile boundaries.
    rs = [r for r in range(h) if any(v not in (1, 9) for v in grid[r])]
    cs = [c for c in range(w) if any(grid[r][c] not in (1, 9) for r in range(h))]
    # At each marked row, sample each 4-column period at its first cell.
    # Include unmarked positions between the colored columns as 9.
    out = []
    for r in rs:
        row = []
        for c in range(3, w, 4):
            row.append(grid[r][c] if grid[r][c] not in (1, 9) else 9)
        out.append(row)
    # Likewise include blank marker rows between the observed rows, sampled
    # at the same 4-row interval.
    return out
